messages:
incident-bot: Page: p99 SLO breach detected for customer Lyrebird (dedicated-pool: lyrebird-euw3-01). metric=inference_p99_latency > 2.0s for 15m. Incident ID INC-173654. runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-pool-latency
Akira (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm on it. Adding SRE and platform.
Javier (SRE): Jumping in — I can see queue_time spikes and kernel stalls in the runtime logs. Tailing /var/log/runtime/lyrebird-*.
Maya (Platform): Confirmed queue build on lyrebird-euw3-01. Autoscaler is capped by reserved capacity per contract, so it won't scale beyond pool size.
Caroline (CS): FYI Lyrebird CS reported slow responses in EU-facing apps. Customer impact estimate: ~20% of requests degraded UX (slow, not errors). They've opened ticket #8873.
Thomas (Support): Got the ticket screenshots. Customer asked if we can throttle background batch jobs; they said they can't stop them right now.
Akira (oncall): Short plan: 1) isolate noisy tenant (ID 1121) from the dedicated pool, 2) gradual traffic-shift to fallback pool lyrebird-euw3-burst, 3) enable KV cache warmups and consider model-variant fallback. Who can run tenant isolation?
Leo (eng-runtime): I can do tenant isolation. Preparing eviction command now.
Leo (eng-runtime): Running:
```
rctl tenant-isolate --tenant 1121 --from-pool lyrebird-euw3-01 --to-pool quarantine-eu3-01 --reason "noisy-large-batches"
```
Javier (SRE): Seeing GPU mem-copy latency spikes on worker-7 around the same time as p99 climbs. Also seeing long GC pauses in the runtime metrics.
Akira (oncall): Caroline, please notify the customer: we'll try routing mitigations that may cause short-lived routing changes. ETA for first update: ~15m.
Caroline (CS): Message to customer sent: "We're aware and working on mitigation. You may see routing shifts for a short window; we'll update in ~15m."
Maya (Platform): Initiating weighted traffic-shift to fallback pool in 20% steps. Command:
```
routing shift --service lyrebird-euw3 --from lyrebird-euw3-01 --to lyrebird-euw3-burst --step 20 --wait 60s
```
deploy-bot: Routing change started for lyrebird-euw3: step 1/5 -> +20% to lyrebird-euw3-burst.
Thomas (Support): Customer replied: "App still slow but noticeably better." They included a p95 snapshot: reduced from 3.2s -> 1.8s.
Javier (SRE): After tenant isolation + step1 traffic shift, p95 down ~35% but p99 still elevated. Worker-7 logs show kernel selection fallback thrashing when quantized model path engaged.
Leo (eng-runtime): Proposal: route Lyrebird tenant to model variant ft-11-quantized-v2 on the burst pool (cached there) — should reduce per-token latency. Need CS approval per contract for variant change.
Caroline (CS): Reached out to customer; they approved trying the quantized variant temporarily.
Akira (oncall): Applying model-route for tenant 9981 now:
```
model-route set --tenant 9981 --model ft-11-quantized-v2 --pool lyrebird-euw3-burst
```
deploy-bot: Model route update applied for tenant 9981 -> ft-11-quantized-v2 on lyrebird-euw3-burst.
Maya (Platform): Note: we hit reserved capacity; requesting human approval to burst to shared capacity for 30m. Akira, can you authorize?
Akira (oncall): Approved: allow burst to shared capacity for 30m for lyrebird-euw3. Monitor closely.
Javier (SRE): After variant switch + burst allowance, p99 dropped to ~1.1s and error rate stable. This looks contained.
incident-bot: Status update: INC-173654 -> CONTAINED. Severity: Sev2. Postmortem required.
Caroline (CS): Updating customer: "Issue contained. You should see normal UX now. We'll follow up with RCA and next steps."
Leo (eng-runtime): I'll collect kernel selection traces, model quantization metrics, and worker-level histograms and post to #eng-runtime for RCA.
Akira (oncall): Handoff: assigning follow-up to Javier (SRE) for RCA & action items. I'll update rotation handoff docs. Thanks team :thumbsup:
